### THE LAW (sub_360C0 :42892, the 3x3 height smoother)

**THE QUAD GATE'S INDEX ARITHMETIC IS SIGNED 32-BIT, NOT u16**
(:42912-19): retail computes `(u16)a1 − 257 / − 256 / − 1` as int and
indexes `mapTerrainType` with the result, so for a ROW-0 cell
(t < 257) the two "row −1" gate reads land BELOW the type plane — in
the SOUND-DRIVER globals at CC0DF..CC1DF (word_CC070 / byte_CC0C2 /
dword_CC126, the HMI init block). Whether a row-0 cell smooths is
decided by sound-driver bytes, NOT by the wrapped row-255 terrain the
port consulted. Only the gate escapes: the 3x3 SUM casts per access
(`(u16)result`, :42928) and wraps correctly; the write is in-plane.
Port model: `Gen::OOB_TYPE_SHIM`, a 257-byte below-plane table —
offsets {56, 59, 71} building-classed (71 = the first byte of
dword_CC126, a static-after-boot sound-init parameter), all else
plain. With the shim, the FULL 441-cell post-collapse height grid at
t=21282 reproduces retail **441/441** (verified offline against the
take's own delta); the wrapped gate left 20 cells adrift: (66,0)
skipped at 145 where retail smooths it to 157 (the type-11 keep wall
at (65,255) sits in the port's old quad but retail never reads it),
(56,0)/(58,0)/(59,0)/(70,0)/(71,0) smoothed where retail's shim bytes
gate them OFF, everything else ±1/2 smoother-order cascade. The
graded head was pure derivative: the mass-fire-spread fires standing
on the rim (slots 601/602/942/989/995) read their z off the drifted
cells; from t=21293 the level-2 repaint painter drags all rubble to
its floor goals and the whole neighborhood re-converges — a ~23-tick
divergence window that cost 200+ boundaries.

Pinned by `features.rs::the_row0_smoother_gate_reads_below_the_type_
plane` (reversion-probed: with the wrapped quad restored the unit
FAILS and the horizon drops 21483 → 21281 on the old sig).

### METHOD

- ⭐⭐⭐ **DUMP THE TRUTH CHANNEL'S OWN DELTA BEFORE THEORISING ABOUT A
  WRITER** — the new `MGC_TERRAIN_DELTA_DUMP=t0:t1` instrument
  (mgc-formats `TerrainImage::dump_delta`, applied in replay) prints
  each tick's recorded (plane, cell, old→new) rows: the changed-cell
  SET killed every "single missing +12 write" theory (the real
  divergence was 20 cells with BOTH signs) and the per-tick delta

- ⭐⭐⭐ **SIMULATE THE PASS OFFLINE AND SEARCH VARIANTS**: with
  post-walk state from the [clp] trace and retail finals from the
  delta, a 30-line python re-implementation of the epilogue scored
  every visit-order/quad/buffering variant — all structurally sane
  variants were WORSE than the port (20 vs 100+ mismatches), which is
  what said "the algorithm is right, the INPUTS differ" and pointed
  at the only row where an index goes negative.
- ⭐⭐ **THE MIXED SMOOTH/SKIP PATTERN WAS THE FINGERPRINT**: retail
  skipped {56,58,59,70,71} and smoothed {57,60,66,67,69} on one row —

### 1. ⭐⭐ THE ROW-0 SMOOTHER SHIM HAS TWO MORE BUILDING BYTES: 63, 65

Session 55 established that `sub_360C0`'s quad gate indexes
`mapTerrainType` **signed-32** (:42912-19), so a row-0 cell reads two
bytes BELOW the plane — sound-driver memory at CC117..CC126, modelled
by `Gen::OOB_TYPE_SHIM`. It fitted `{56, 59, 71}` and warned that a
later take might extend it. mc1hwl0 t=24739 is that take, and the
reason it took two sessions is worth keeping:

**A cell only exercises its shim bytes once its FOUR IN-PLANE READS
PASS.** t=21282's collapse was 16 wide (x 56..71) but its build
stream SKIPPED (62..65,0), so those cells kept building types
12/27/27/79, failed the gate on their own type, and never touched
shim 62..66. "(57..69,0) all pass" was therefore a statement about the
cells the stream reached, not about the table. t=24739 is castle 233's
SECOND collapse, an 8x8 footprint (x 60..67) that DOES rubble them and
retiles them to type 1 — and retail STILL declines to smooth (62,0),
(64,0), (65,0) while smoothing (61,0) and (66,0). 61 and 66 smoothing
forces shim 62/66/67 plain, which forces **63 and 65 building**. (64
stays plain: 65 already explains (64,0)'s skip and nothing observed
pins it.) No temporal variation is needed — one static table still
serves both collapses 3,457 ticks apart, which is the first real test
"static after boot" has had.

The consequence is the head. (64,0) keeps its knock-down 163 instead
of averaging to 150, so `sub_47130`'s `sub_11F50` under the castle
reads 5216 not 4800; every spill ball's `+46` is born

gravity the nine (10,39) balls sit at z 6184 against our 6132. Rows
253..255 of the same footprint always matched — the smoother walks
y ascending from 252, so row 0's error only ever propagated
FORWARD, into rows 1 and 2.

Method note: the port's own `[clp]` trace and
`MGC_TERRAIN_DELTA_DUMP` are a matched pair — one gives the port's

The one surviving deviation is the human's respawn. Retail's human
dies at ~43095, lands (`+70` 3) by 43135; scancode 57 first appears on
record **43137** and retail respawns at **43138**. Our recovery reads
the Space lane off the pair's END record, so we respawn at 43137 —

manifestations re-mint.

**The obvious fix is wrong.** Every other MC1 lane in
`recover_pair_mc1` reads the START record (`move_byte = pw.move_bits`,

respawning at 7629, on the record it appears on. The two sites
disagree by one tick under either rule. MC1's turn loop is not
frame-locked, so the per-record key snapshot carries a genuine ±1
turn of jitter; this is the documented dating caveat cashing out, not
a port law. Reverted, and recorded here so the next reader does not
re-derive it.

### LAW A — THE DEATH LANDING DISCARDS THE TOP VICTIM CELL

`mc1hwl0` t=31888, banked since session 69 with EVERY predicate fix
refuted. The banked hypothesis was right and the answer was not a
predicate at all.

The last statement of the fall handler `sub_45FC0` is a BARE decrement
of the recycle stack's top index — `--*(_DWORD *)(result + 4593)`
(hw :51637). The shipped binaries carry it verbatim as
`ff 88 f1 11 00 00` = `decl 0x11f1(%eax)` at **HIDDEN 0x466DF** and
**CARPET 0x4639F**, immediately before the epilogue, and it is the
ONLY bare `--top` in either image (every other writer is the rebuild
at 0x375F8, the seizure's own post-decrement, or a full `movl $-1`
disarm). It is unconditional on the landing path: the one branch that
skips it (0x463CC) is the branch that also skips the rebuild.

It is a pure DISCARD — no killer call, no class wipe. The dropped
record stays alive; it just stops being the next victim. So the port
performs `Vec::pop()`, never `mc2_recycle_pop` (which skips invalid
cells, counts a seizure, and hands the caller a record to kill).
Landed at both port mirrors of that one shared retail function —
`mc1/rivals.rs::rival_death_impact` and `engine/world.rs::player_land`
— positioned AFTER the grave spawn, matching 0x4663A → 0x466DF.

⭐⭐⭐ WHY EVERY PREDICATE FIX WAS REFUTED. The port's victim stack was
retail's stack plus exactly one trailing cell (515 vs 514). Under the
descending scan slot 36 is pushed BEFORE slot 16, so 36 sits mid-stack
in BOTH and 16 lands above retail's top. There was never a predicate
that could separate slot 16 from slot 36 — and none was needed. Three
sessions of predicate hunting were looking at the wrong half of the
data structure: the CONTENT was right, the TOP was wrong.

Unit-pinned (`the_death_landing_discards_the_top_recycle_victim`) —
a pair fixture is STRUCTURALLY BLIND, because both allocator halves
are ungraded lanes and pair mode reinstalls retail's stack every pair.
That is exactly why it hid for so long.

EFFECT: **mc1hwl0 world 31,887 → 37,109 (+5,222)**; **app 32,879 →
38,708 (+5,829)**.

### LAW B — THE RINGS ARE A DATA FILE, NOT A FORMULA

`mc1l32-quick` t=34181 `missing(10,0)slot567`, the highest-value head
on the board.

Retail's mana-ball merge partner search `sub_11D10` (:17127-73) walks
rings 0..=(f80+255)>>8 through the iterator `sub_11410`/`sub_114B0`
(:16697/:16732), whose offsets are **read from `DATA/SEARCH.DAT`**
(loaded by `sub_11540`, :16783-815) — a 32x32 Euclidean-band ring
image. Those shells are 2x2-ANCHORED, not Chebyshev squares:

    ring 0 = (0,0) (+1,0) (0,+1) (+1,+1)      — a 2x2 BLOCK
    ring 1 = the 12 cells of the -1..+2 border

So retail reaches one column/row FURTHER in +x/+y than a square of the
same index, and at larger radii it is ROUND where a square visits
corners retail never does. The scan takes the FIRST admissible overlap
and STOPS, so ORDER is as load-bearing as membership.

At t=34181 ball 693 (base cell 192,244) meets slot 777 at offset
(+1,+1) — retail's RING 0 — while the square model reached slot 567 at
(-1,0) first and merged the wrong partner (mana retail 9000/2390 vs
port 4430/5760), which displaced the tick's new (10,0) spawn from slot
567 to 897. The spawn itself was never missing.

The fix is `Gen::ring_cells`, which IS the real SEARCH.DAT iterator
(carrying retail's dropped-last-cell off-by-one) and was ALREADY in
use by the certified sibling scan `sub_11AC0` with identical centre
and radius arithmetic. `combat.rs:6036` was the last hand-rolled
Chebyshev ring left in `mgc-sim` — grep-confirmed.

EFFECT: **mc1l32-quick world 34,180 → END (41,600 clean, devs=0)** and
**app 41,600 bit-exact throughout**. ✅ **mc1l32-quick IS CERTIFIED.**
The app head t=34703 was carried exactly as session 69 predicted.

Fixture `the-ball-merge-partner-scan-walks-the-search-dat-rings`
(t=34180). Reversion-probed: the square arm reproduces
`extra:10,39` + `missing:10,0` and the other 39 mc1l32 fixtures stay
green, so the pin is specific as well as non-vacuous.

### LAW C — A REFUSED BLOOM LEAVES THE CARRIER ALIVE

`mc1hwl0` t=37110 `(9,12)slot983:flags`, retail 6 / port 1030.

The (9,12) lightning-storm carrier's self-kill sits INSIDE the (10,38)
cloud's null guard. HIDDEN `0x54441 test %eax,%eax` / `0x54443 je
0x544ba` jumps straight to the epilogue, PAST the kill at 0x544B2 —
and that kill, `sub_41E80_421C0` @ 0x421C0, is a two-instruction leaf:
`mov 0x4(%esp),%eax; orb $0x4,0x11(%eax); ret`, i.e. flags |= 0x400.
So when `new_event` refuses (free stack AND recycle stack both dry)
the carrier is NOT marked dead: it stays alive and re-tries its bloom.
Decompile hw :59852-73, base :63768-88. The port set the flag one line
BELOW the closing brace.

⚠⚠ THE FORK IS DELIBERATE AND DOES NOT GENERALISE. Twenty bytes
earlier in the SAME function the WATER arm spawns its splash and kills
UNCONDITIONALLY — its `je 0x54407` skips only the +24 copy, and the
kill at 0x54408 stands outside (the port's `splash_and_die` already
matches that shape). CARPET.EXE carries both shapes identically, so
this is shared MC1/HW, not an HW fork. The port has ~44
`flags |= 0x400` sites in `mc1/combat.rs` alone; any that pair an
unconditional kill with a spawn retail guards will misfire the same
way, and this take keeps hitting them while the pool is starved.
BANKED as a per-site audit against the binary — NOT a blanket rule,
because retail itself is not consistent.

EFFECT: **mc1hwl0 world 37,109 → 42,647 (+5,538)**, new head t=42648
`(5,4)slot924:target_yaw`.

Fixture `a-refused-storm-bloom-leaves-the-carrier-alive` (t=37109).
Pair mode CAN see this one: retail's free stack is len 5 at t=37109,
so the import hands the port a non-empty pool and the port drains it
to 0 inside the graded tick. Reversion-probed: `field:9,12:flags`,
exactly one fixture.

### ⭐⭐⭐ RULES THIS SESSION PROVED

- **WHEN EVERY PREDICATE IS REFUTED, THE PREDICATE IS NOT THE BUG.**
  Law A's stack had the right CONTENTS and the wrong TOP. Three
  sessions of "which entity test separates slot 16 from slot 36" were
  asking a question with no answer, because the two records are
  byte-identical and retail's own stack contains both. The diagnostic
  that ended it was reading the two stacks side by side and noticing
  the port's was retail's with one cell APPENDED — a `Vec::pop`
  signature, visible the moment the MC1 dump printed the recycle half.
- **THE SHIPPED EXE SETTLES WHAT THE LISTING ONLY SUGGESTS — AND
  SOMETIMES AGREES WITH IT.** All three of this session's binary
  checks CONFIRMED the decompile (`:51637`, `:59852-73`, the 0x20400
  mask and scan direction). The value was not catching a corruption;
  it was converting "the listing says so" into "the instruction is
  there", which is what let Law A and Law C land without a hedge.
  ⭐ The corroboration that mattered most was the NEGATIVE one: the
  water arm 20 bytes from the cloud arm, which proved the null guard
  was a deliberate fork rather than a compiler artifact and stopped
  the law from being over-generalised across 44 sites.
- **RETAIL'S RING GEOMETRY IS SHIPPED DATA.** Any "neighbourhood
  scan" in this engine is `SEARCH.DAT` unless proven otherwise; a
  hand-rolled Chebyshev square is a bug even when the radius matches,
  because the shells are 2x2-anchored and the walk STOPS at the first
  hit. When porting such a scan, look for an already-certified
  sibling using `Gen::ring_cells` and copy it.
- **⚠ DO NOT REBUILD WHILE A GATE SWEEP IS RUNNING.** A mid-sweep
  `cargo build --release` swapped the binary under a running
  certified sweep, leaving its tail measured against a different build
  than its head. Caught and re-run cleanly; the mixed run was
  discarded rather than reported.

## SESSION 71 — RETAIL ASKS THE ROSTER; THE PORT ASKED THE POOL

Focused mode, mc1hwl0 + mc1l32-quick (the charter's two re-takes).
Three laws landed, and **mc1hwl0 is CERTIFIED** — END under
`mgc-conform replay` and bit-exact under the app, on both instruments,
53,043 graded ticks. mc1l32-quick re-confirmed END on both. That makes
**12 certified takes** and closes the re-take push.

All three laws are the same mistake in three places: retail asks a
LINKED ROSTER a question and the port asked the POOL. The rosters are
`str_36382x[0..20]` (the per-model class-5 chains, wizext 36382 + 4·m),
rebuilt at tick top with `class == 5 ∧ act ≥ 0 ∧ state ≠ 120` and
**memset wholesale by a NewEvent SEIZURE** (:43885-91). The port has
carried `MobChains` — membership, order, per-slot cut AND the seizure
blank — since session 42. These three call sites simply never used it.

### LAW A — the pack separation scan walks the chain (mc1/mobs.rs)

`sub_1A390`'s separation loop (remc1 :21796, remc1hw :20346 —
byte-identical, two witnesses) loads `str_36382x[+65]` and follows `+0`
(`v13 = *(_DWORD *)v13`) down to the pool base. Its ONLY per-member
test is `+24 != own id`: class, model, state and life are membership,
sampled once at tick top, never re-read live. The port ran a full-array
walk with live `class/model/state/life` filters — wrong in both
directions (it sees a creature the rebuild did not, it hides one that
died mid-tick) and, decisively, blind to the seizure blank.

mc1hwl0 t=42648 is the seizure: the volcano plume drains free 10 → 0
and recycle 793 → 352 (441 records seized), so every roster walk
dispatched after the seizing slot sees an EMPTY list. Retail's militia
924 therefore keeps its leader bearing to slot 34 (`+34` = 728 =
`angle_of(1388, 1086)`); the array scan found militia 236 one tile east
(dx 214, dy 26) and turned away from it (1575).
**World 42,647 → 47,079.**

### LAW B — the Undead Army ring belongs to the (10,36) spawner

The bolt does not raise the ring. The (9,11) undead-army projectile is
minted with `+68/+69` = 10/36 (:65959-60), so the detonation's
generic-explode child is `sub_3B3E0`'s **(10,36) spawner** (:47370 —
state 38, life 8, `+44` = −1536, sprite 41, extents 512), and
`sub_26E90` (:29353) raises the eight skeletons on THAT record's own
dispatch, later in the same slot walk. Three sub-laws came with it:

- **The ring size is the free-pool depth.** `v9 = sub_37710_37AD0()`
  (:44061 = `free.len() + 1`), negative-clamped, capped at 8, then
  capped again at `64 − live`. The port hardcoded 8.
- **The live census walks the model-9 chain** (:29373 loads
  `str_36382x[9]` at 36418) and tests `+144 == owner` alone — no

- **The owner rides `+144` ALONE.** remc1 :29399 writes no `+24`, and

  friendly-fire hunch, flagged in-comment as a suspected transcription

The spawner taking a pool slot of its own is what the horizon actually

**World 47,079 → 50,148.**

### LAW C — the kill trigger probes the roster HEAD, not a census

`sub_59E40_5A350` (:67460) dereferences `str_36382x[model]` in both
arms — `!*(_DWORD *)(dword_AE408 + 4·a2 + 36382)` for a named model
(:67492) and the same load inside the `a2 == −1` scan (:67472). The
port counted a live census with the very predicate the tick-top rebuild
uses, which is why it survived so long: **on a quiet tick the two agree
exactly.** They part on a seizure tick, where the heads are memset and
every trigger dispatched afterwards reads its watched model as EXTINCT
with the monsters alive and well.

mc1hwl0's slot-37 m3 watcher pins it end to end. Retail's `+26` sits at
**12** by t=50130 — four countdown steps the port never took — with TEN
model-3 corpses still in the pool at t=50133, and the counter cashes out
at t=50149: sound 41, the disposition fires, the trigger despawns, and
the death-landing-class free-list rebuild (`sub_37220` :43825, the
DESCENDING 999→1 scan) re-sorts the stack so retail's next allocations
take slots 1/3/5 while the port's incremental stack handed them back to
the freed high slots — re-ticking records ahead of the walk and
cascading into 70 extra live entities in one tick. The port's `+26`
never left 0 for the whole 53,053-tick take.
**World 50,148 → END; app 43,703 → END.**

### HOW THE HEAD WAS FOUND (the instrument story)

The t=50149 head was INHERITED — the pair at 50148→50149 is CLEAN — and
the entity-set channel showed a 70-record blow-out with no field
divergence to explain it. `dump-state --port`'s allocator line
(session 70's tooling debt) is what cracked it: free stacks agree
byte-for-byte at t=50147 and t=50148 and then read `retail len 728 tail
[14,13,12,11,10,9,7,6]` against `port len 661 tail [662,666,…,701]` —
a DESCENDING tail is the rebuild's signature and nothing else in the
engine produces one. From there the only ungraded lane in the whole
tick was the trigger's `+26` (retail 1, port 5 at t=50148), and
`MGC_WRITE_TRACE=37:f26` showed the port's counter had never been
written before t=50130.

⭐⭐⭐ **AN UNGRADED LANE CAN CARRY A 50,000-TICK DEBT.** `+26` on one
class-11 record is not in `EntObsMc1`, so nothing graded it for the
whole take; the divergence only became visible when the counter cashed
out into an allocator rebuild. The raw-shadow census exists for exactly
this and was not the thing that found it — the ALLOCATOR TAIL was.

⭐⭐ **WHEN A COUNTER IS OFF BY N, COUNT THE TICKS IT DID NOT STEP.**
The port's `+26` and retail's differ by 4 at t=50148, and the fix is
not in the counter — it is in the four ticks on which retail's probe
said "extinct" and the port's said "alive". Reconstructing which four
named the probe.

⭐ **THREE CALL SITES, ONE MISSING ABSTRACTION.** After Law A the
second and third heads were the same question asked twice more. Once a
data structure turns out to be the answer, grep every consumer of the
thing it replaces before measuring again.

## SESSION 81 — THE LEASH, THE MAILBOX HOP, AND A REGISTER WHOSE LANE WAS THERE ALL ALONG

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore`
CERTIFIED and held at END; **`mc2l6-rival-spells-galore` 1376 -> the
session's close**; `mc2l0-spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched).
FIVE laws off one head chain — 1377 -> 1625 -> 1657 — the first two
the duel ENFORCEMENT that session 80's lock made reachable for the
first time.

### A — `sub_5DE30` IS INSIDE THE MOVER, AND EVERY OPERAND WAS A DIFFERENT ONE

Head: mc2l6-rsg t=1377, `pose:pose.x,pose.y,pose.yaw` (retail 52905 /
13192 / 1167, port 52906 / 13191 / 1164). The duel enforcement had been
a tick-head pass writing the world's KNOCK channel — a standing
DEVIATIONS approximation, "magnitude formula traced, transport ours."
Retail's seat is `sub_5D530` EF:59721, i.e. INSIDE the carpet's own
mover, between the one-shot displacement mailbox (block 6) and the
debuff decay (block 8), and its tail is:

```
v12 = 3 * a1x->minSpeed_0x84_132 / 2;
LOWORD(v6) = (v5 - type160->dword_0x142_322) / (1024 / (int16)v12);
if ((int16)v6 < -(int16)v12) v6 = 3 * a1x->minSpeed_0x84_132 / -2;
if ((int16)v6 >  (int16)v12) LOWORD(v6) = v12;
v7 = tan2(a1x->pos, v2x->pos);  v8 = v7;
v9 = a1x->yaw + sub_58350(a1x->yaw, v7, 5, 0x82);  HIBYTE(v9) &= 7u;
a1x->yaw = v9;
MoveEntity_57FA0(&predictedAxis, v8, a1x->pitch_0x1E_30, v6);
```

Five separate corrections, and the head needed the transport AND the
operands together:

- **The metric is 3-D.** `v5 = sub_583F0_distance_3d` (EF:59916), and
  the HELD distance the delta is taken against is the same 3-D call at
  the stamp (`sub_5EFA0` EF:60650). The port measured both on the
  ground plane, so a duel fought at altitude held its shadow.
- **The cap and the divisor are CONSTANTS.** `minSpeed_0x84_132` on a
  wizard is `x_DWORD_D4B8C` = 80, stamped by `AddPlayer03_00_5E010`
  (EF:59958) and never rewritten on a wizard's path — so `v12` is 120
  and `1024 / v12` is 8, every tick, for every duel. The port derived
  both from how fast the carpet happened to be flying
  (`player.speed.max(16)`), which is a different number on almost every
  tick and never 120 (the carpet's own ceiling is 80).
- **The clamp is SIGNED.** Inside the held distance retail SHOVES THE
  CASTER BACK OUT at up to −120; the port's `.clamp(0, cap)` could only
  ever reel him in.
- **The yaw servo was missing entirely.** `sub_58350(yaw, bearing, 5,
  0x82)` — [`Gen::turn_step`], cap 130 — rewrites the caster's heading
  every tick of the lock, and `moveBoost` has no yaw authority at all,
  so the knock channel could not have carried it. This is the head's
  own lane: retail's 1167 IS the bearing to rival 370, reached in one
  servo step from the port's un-servoed 1164.
- **The step's heading is the RAW bearing `v8`, not the servoed yaw**,
  and its pitch is `a1x->pitch_0x1E_30` — the published aim pitch. The
  carpet is dragged sideways in three dimensions while it slews to face
  its opponent.

Retail's liveness set is exactly three tests — the manifestation
charged, `v2x->life_0x8 >= 0`, `v5 < range` — where the port also
required class 3, the free bit clear and the rival not eliminated.
Three port inventions, deleted.

Landed as [`crate::flight::mc2_move`] block 7 (the comment there was
the standing "UNPORTED (banked, worklist 7)" note): the world computes
bearing + signed pull at the dispatch, the mover applies the servo and
the polar step onto the CANDIDATE so the commit gate can still refuse
it and nothing survives into the next tick. **1376 -> ~1594** on its
own, and the head moved BACKWARD one tick — which was law B.

⚠ On a PINNED-POSE turn (`tick_pose_pair`, `World::tick`) there is no
candidate to displace, so the enforcement still runs for its state half
— the range/liveness break and the opponent's drain — and drops the
leash. The pair channel is structurally blind to the leash either way:
`word_0x146_326` / `dword_0x142_322` / `word_0x14A_330` are not in the
MC2 import, so an imported world never holds a lock. UNIT PIN.

### C — THE HUMAN LIFE-REGEN REGISTER, MC2 COLUMN (the banked item)

Head: mc2l6-rsg t=1625, `(3,0)slot343:life` — retail 7715, port 7750.
`player_regen_block` credited MC1 with the STORED rate and MC2 with the
FRESHLY SELECTED one, under this rationale: *"MC2 keeps the fresh-select
rate: its recorder lane for the register is undecoded, so an unseeded
stale value would regress every regen pair."*

**The lane was decoded all along.** `Mc2Wizard::life_regen` lifts
`lifeRegen_0x163_355` at flight +355 (mgcr.rs), and its own doc comment
in mgc-formats states the applied-then-selected law verbatim. What was
missing was the SEAT: `retail_import_mc2`'s human `Player` literal
never read it, where the MC1 arm has carried `life_rate: wiz.life_rate`
for months. So the stale-value objection was true of the code and false
of the recording.

## SESSION 78 — FOUR LAWS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT WHOSE VALUE A SITE READS

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore`
CERTIFIED and held at END; **mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 686 → 843**;
`mc2l0-spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). Four laws, all landed
in the main session, all off the ONE head chain t=687 → 761 → 764 →
784: each law's landing exposed the next.

⭐⭐⭐ **THREE OF THE FOUR ARE "WHOSE VALUE", NOT "WHAT VALUE".** The
lock range is read off the OWNER and the port read the projectile; the
scan radius is read off the writer's own extents with NO floor and the
port floored it; the life regen is read off a STORED register and the
port recomputed it fresh. Session 76's "right number, wrong outcome ⇒
ask which slot the write lands on" has a sibling: **right shape, wrong
outcome ⇒ ask whose record the operand comes off.**

### THE LAWS

- **A — THE CLASS-3 LOCK RANGE IS THE OWNER'S BEHAVIOUR ROW, NOT THE
  PROJECTILE'S.** `sub_67CB0` hoists `v43x = Entities[a1x->id_0x1A_26]`
  before the wizard walk and gates every candidate on
  `sub_583F0_distance_3d(cand, self) <= v43x->dword_0xA0_160x->
  word_160_0x1c_28` (EF:54783-88; the sibling cases hoist the same way
  at EF:54866/54941). Every class-9 row carries 4096 — which is why
  reading it off the shot looked harmless — but every wizard ctor
  carries **8192** (`AddPlayer_4A920` → `str_D7BD6[66]`, cave `[104]`;
  `sub_4A9C0` → `[67]`), so a WIZARD-cast bolt locks a full 4096 further
  than the port allowed. mc2l6 t=687: rival 370's fresh (9,0), muzzled
  at the caster's x/y with `z += array_0x52_82.fov` = 930, sits 5,065
  from rival 383 — inside 8192, outside 4096. Retail locks it
  (`word_0x96_150` 383), `sub_655C0` writes the desired aim into the
  `roll`/`fov` pair (578 / 3 — the pitch is 3 and not −10 because
  `sub_65580` RAISES the victim by its own box first), then
  `sub_65C20`'s one-shot arm turns yaw by the hard-capped 34 (515 →

  ⚠ The human owner is out of the pool and has no `row156`; all three
  wizard rows carry 8192, so the constant fallback is exact, not an

  `sub_583F0(&ix->position, &ix->position)` is a remc2 SOURCE typo and

- **B — THERE IS NO FLOOR UNDER THE ch0 AREA SCAN RADIUS, IN EITHER
  GAME.** `sub_10C80`'s ch0 tile pass runs `for i = -v24; i <= v24` with

## SESSION 77 — THE MC2 PLAYER BLOCK HAD NEVER BEEN LOOKED AT

Focus = the galores. `mc1l0-spells-galore` CERTIFIED and held at END;

the instrument then handed over every law it landed.

### THE INSTRUMENT — `wiz_shadow_mc2`

`MGC_RAW_SHADOW`'s report had, for as long as MC2 has been graded,
printed this instead of numbers:

> WIZEXT SHADOW: NOT WATCHED on this game — no `wiz_shadow_mc2` and no
> port-side MC2 player-lane projection exist … Its own dig.

So the entire MC2 rival brain — `ai_state`, `burst`, the 26 recast
cooldowns, the hate ledger and its war flags, the weave and water-steer
FSMs, the cast-charge meter, the stored castle index, the spell book —
was UNGRADED on both instruments. The recording carries the whole
2124-byte player block per wizard and `retail_import_mc2` restores it
every pair, so none of it could ever fail a pair either.

Built this session (`World::wiz_shadow_mc2` +
`Mc2Rival::wiz_shadow_lanes` + `Shadow::compare_wiz_mc2` + the
`norm_retail_ai_state_mc2` collapse, wired into BOTH the free-run and
the pair paths), plus the brain half of `dump-state <t> wiz` so the
lanes can be read absolutely and not just as mismatch rows. First run
over 600 ticks of mc2l6: **3,588 mismatches across 17 lanes**, the
earliest at t=1.

⭐⭐⭐ **A "NOT WATCHED" LINE IS A DIG, AND IT PAYS ON THE FIRST RUN.**
Every law below came out of that first census — the head at t=587 had
been diagnosed-but-not-landed by session 76 as "a genuinely new dig,
budget a session for the selector"; the instrument named the handler in
one `dump-state` call instead.

### THE LAWS

- **A — THE LONG WAY HOME IS A MANA RUN.** `sub_133B0`'s castle-EXISTS

  → walk spell 1 (Possession / Mana Magnet / Mana Lock) DOWN from its

- **B — THE APPROACH RING IS COMPARED IN LINEAR UNITS, NOT SQUARED

  target)` against its raw a3/a4 radii, and that function (Maths:738-45)

## SESSION 74 — THE MC2 HEAL DIG, AND A SPELL THE PORT NEVER CAST

Focus = the two remaining galores plus the banked MC2 heal dig (player

instrument too; every other uncertified row byte-held; suite **659/0**;
**292 fixtures, 0 regressions**; clippy 0; fmt.

⭐⭐⭐ **THE SESSION'S SHAPE: A PLAYER REPORT THAT WAS A COMPOSITE OF
TWO GAMES.** SESSION 73 measured the MC1 half of the player's heal
observation, found the second sentence unreproducible, and named the
mechanism (a terminal release) that made it impossible. It also left an
explicit ⚠⚠ ambiguity: the player added *"I have tested this in mc2 and
it worked"*, and it was unresolved whether they meant retail or the
port. **Both readings turned out to be right about different things.**
The port has no MC2 heal at all (so it cannot have been our build), and
retail MC2 *does* behave the way the player guessed — because MC2 and
MC1 put the same life test on **opposite sides of the same admission**.
⭐ Resolve an ambiguity by measuring BOTH candidates; "the player is
describing one game" was the assumption that hid a second law.

### LAW A — THE RIVAL'S CASTLE-LESS FIRST CASTLE IS FREE

`sub_12FE0`'s `case 2u` (EF:6822-40) has two legs and only one reaches
`sub_5F660` — which is where the manifestation arm AND the mana debit
live (`sub_5F7B0` past the `mana < maxMana` refusal, EF:60948-56). With
a castle standing the upgrade leg calls it and pays. Castle-LESS,
retail calls `IfSubtypeCallCreatingManaSphere_4A190(&axis, 3, 2)`,
stamps `id_0x1A_26` and `CastleEntityIndex_0x3A_58`, and returns 1: no
arm, no recast cooldown, **no payment**.

The port had already read the cooldown half of that (its comment says
so in as many words) and still charged for the spawn — the shape
SESSION 73 named, a law landed on one half of its own mechanism.

Witness: mc2l6-rsg t=70, rival 378 mints its first castle. Retail's
purse never moves — `mana` pinned at 1000 (= `mana_max`) with `d88`
+100 from t=71 to the end of the take — while the port billed the whole

`(3,1)slot378:mana`. **70 → 245.**

### LAW B — THE RIVAL'S CAST FRAME *IS* THE WINDOW'S FIRST TICK

`sub_5F7B0` (EF:60974) is a bare `word_0x2E_46 = word_0x30_48` at the
CASTER's walk slot — and MC2 mints a wizard's 26 manifestations at
slots ABOVE it (mc2l6's rival 370 owns 371-377). So the class-15

word_0x30_48`, stamps `sub_68DE0`'s first-tick debit and decrements.

The port stamps that debit at the cast site but runs the countdown from

the full duration bought one extra tick and shifted the mid-burst regen
pin a frame late.

Instrument, mc2l6 t=244, the fireball (`f30` = 5): retail's counter
reads 4/3/2/1/0 across t=244..248 and holds `d88` at 0 for 245-248,
back to +100 at 249. The port read 5/4/3/2/1/0 and spent t=245 on its

own slot (`mc2_rival_manifestation_tick`), so it already gets the

that would have been eaten.

⭐⭐ **`f26` IN THE PORT IS NOT `f2e` IN `dump-state`.** The dump names
lanes by BYTE OFFSET, so the token's `word_0x2E_46` prints as `f2e`;
the port's *field* called `f26` is a different thing entirely. Reading

— the counter ladder that names the whole bug is in `f2e`/`f30`.

### LAW C — MC2 HEAL IS `sub_6A300`, AND THE PORT HAD NO BODY FOR IT

The banked dig, and it was worse than "approximate": `mc2_spell_fire`'s
spell-5 arm set `player.heal_active`, the window expiry cleared it, and
**nothing in the crate ever read it.** Casting heal in MC2 restored
nothing — the only `player.life` writers were the cheats, the respawn,
the passive regen and MC1's two heal sites. SESSION 73's construction-
level sweep said exactly this; the dig confirms it and supplies the
body.

`sub_6A300` (EF:56430-56477), per tick:

- admit on `sub_68D50` **AND** `mana_0x90_144 >= maxMana_0x8C_140`
  (:56445) — the extra purse leg is UNCONDITIONAL, so unlike every
  other MC2 spell heal re-checks affordability every tick, not just the
  `word_0x2E_46 == word_0x30_48` one. Run dry mid-window and it
  collapses (`+46 = 1`, :56466);
- sound 25 on the first admitted tick, healing or not;
- **then, and only if `life_0x8 < maxLife_0x4`**: the XP award
  (`sub_6D8B0(parent, 5, 1)` :56452, so a full-life cast scores
  nothing), `life += maxLife * subSpellIndex_0x2A_42 / 100` clamped to
  the ceiling, and the **FULL cost stamped on the regen delta**
  (:56458-61) — not the skeleton's one-shot debit at the arm;
- `sub_6A300` never calls `sub_68DE0`, so heal pins NO mid-burst regen.

Witness, mc2l0-spells-galore t=22776-86 (hand_left = 5): eleven ticks of

passive regen, which is why the same window reads +100 on the ticks
where a hit had stalled the regen (mc2l6 t=14444).

Pair fixture `mc2-heal-is-sub-6a300-per-tick-heal-and-full-cos` grades
t=22777; under the reverted build it reads `life: retail 7735 port
7635` — the port banking only the passive +5.

### LAW D — AND THE RIVAL COLUMN RUNS THE SAME BODY

Retail's is caster-generic (it resolves its wizard through the token's
`parentId_0x28_40`), so there is one heal in the engine. The port's
rival arm was a flagged APPROX — a flat `maxLife/20` per armed tick
(MC1's 5%), no life admission, no purse test and **no cost at all**.
Replaced with `sub_6A300`.

That forced a second reading: **the debit is not part of the arm.**
`sub_5F7B0` only writes the counter and two flag bits; the payment is
each effect body's own first-tick `sub_68DE0`, which lands in the same
frame because the token sits above the caster. The port's cast-site
debit is its stand-in for that — and it is WRONG for the one body that
never calls `sub_68DE0`. Heal is now excluded from it and bills itself.

### 🎮 THE PLAYER'S OBSERVATION, RESOLVED ACROSS BOTH GAMES

*"In both games heal costs nothing if there's nothing to heal, no matter
how many times it is cast, even though it appears active. It basically
exchanges mana for health. My guess is that if hurt while heal is
active, it will start costing and healing again."*

The two engines put `actLife < maxLife` on opposite sides of the same
admission:

- **MC1** `sub_56270` (remc1 :65101-03) has it INSIDE — a full-life
  tick takes the `else` and RELEASES (`+48 = 1`). Terminal.
- **MC2** `sub_6A300` (:56445/:56450) admits on the gate and the purse
  alone and NESTS the life test inside the accepted branch. A full-life
  tick does nothing at all — no heal, no XP, no debit — **and the
  window stays open and keeps re-testing.**

So sentence 1 holds in both. Sentence 2 — *"if hurt while heal is
active, it will start costing and healing again"* — is **MC2-only, and
exactly right there**: the live window resumes with no re-cast.
SESSION 73's MC1 finding stands unchanged (there it is the RE-CAST that
looks like a resume), and the ⚠⚠ ambiguity it banked is closed: the
player was describing retail, and the port could not have been the
subject because the port had no MC2 heal to test.

⭐⭐⭐ **A PLAYER REPORT CAN BE RIGHT ABOUT THE OBSERVABLE IN ONE GAME
AND RIGHT ABOUT THE MECHANISM IN THE OTHER.** From the seat MC1 and MC2
are indistinguishable until you are hurt WHILE the window runs — which
is precisely the experiment neither session would have thought to run
without the report.

## SESSION 73 — mc1l0-spells-galore CERTIFIED: THE HALF-LANDED LAWS

`mc1l0-spells-galore` went **2,732 → END (10,747 ticks, devs=0,
segments=1)** on five laws, and is **bit-exact on the app instrument
too**. Thirteenth certified take. Every uncertified row in the corpus
byte-held; suite 550/0; **291 fixtures, 0 regressions**; clippy 0; fmt.

⭐⭐⭐ **THE SESSION'S SHAPE: FOUR OF THE FIVE LAWS WERE ALREADY IN THE
TREE, LANDED ON THE WRONG HALF OF THEIR OWN MECHANISM.** Not one was a
missing decompile read — the citations were sitting in the port's own
comments. What was missing was the *other call site*: a ctor's line
attributed to a cast arm, a token body wired to the strict lane but not
to the native one, twice. **When a law is landed, grep for every path
that reaches the same behaviour before calling it done.**

### LAW A — THE TWO SPRITE-209 LOBS DOUBLE THEIR EXTENTS IN THE CTOR

`sub_39A90` (:45917, possess) and `sub_3A2F0` (:46385, Mana Magnet)
both close with an INLINE `sub_37130_374F0(v2, 2 * +80, 2 * +84)` after
the plain sprite bind — identical in CARPET and HIDDEN (hw:42038 /
hw:42505). Sprite 209 derives 90/90/75, so both fly at **180/180/150**.

The port had the doubling on **possession's CAST arm** instead
(`cast_projectile` id 3 and its rival twin), citing the same :45917.
The misattribution read as a HOLE rather than a wrong value because the
MAGNET shares the ctor and has no cast arm of its own — it flew at half
size for the entire campaign, and `ent_overlap`'s SUMMED extents meant
it passed straight through the ball it was fired at.

⚠ The wrapper `sub_370A0_37460` has exactly three call sites, all m13
arrow — which is what the port's `set_sprite_x2` doc said, correctly.
**The doubling also ships INLINE, and the wrapper's call list cannot
find it.** Grep the SHAPE (`sub_37130_374F0(.., 2 * ..)`), not the
wrapper. ⚠ And `e.f80 *= 2` at a cast site is not idempotent the way
the setter is: leaving both in place double-doubled to 360/360/300 and
cost 1,144 ticks back before it was caught.

Witness: mc1l0-sg slot 46 held retail 180/180/150 vs the port's
90/90/75 **from its first tick (t=2723)** in the raw-shadow census, and
never touched down; retail's terminated at t=2733 into the
(10,12)+(10,54) pair. Horizon 2,732 → (head becomes a flags row).

### LAW B — THE (10,54) MAGNET AND THE (10,55) DEATH FIELD ARE BORN OFF THE TILE CHAIN

`sub_3B970` (:47694-97) and `sub_3BA00` (:47726-29) store `+72`/`+76`
RAW and set `+16 |= 1`; neither calls `sub_41CF0`. The port's `link`
was **invisible on the castle-ejector path** — which relinks 25 tiles
out immediately, so the corpus pin of flags 5 on those magnets is THAT

### LAW C — CLASS-9 STATE 19 IS A ONE-TICK RELAY, NOT A FUSE

`sub_54480_54810` (remc1 :63928-40 = remc1hw :60038-50), bound by the
table read off both shipped EXEs (CARPET 0x9CF34 row 0x13 → 0x54480;
HIDDEN 0x9D134 → 0x54810). Mint the `+68/+69` child at the carrier's
OWN `+72`, copy `+24`/`+30`/`+32`/`+44`, reap ITSELF via `sub_41E80`
**inside the null guard**, and **no `sub_526C0`** — it does not score.

`sub_566C0` (:65266-89) is Rebound's skeleton with a different bit:

Same shape, one spell over. Admission is the shared gate AND

### PLAYER OBSERVATION (same session, post-landing) — HEAL IS FREE WITH NOTHING TO HEAL

Player, unprompted after Law E landed: *"in both games heal costs
nothing if there's nothing to heal, no matter how many times it is
cast, even though it appears active. It basically exchanges mana for
health. My guess is that if hurt while heal is active, it will start
costing and healing again."*

**First half: CONFIRMED, and it is exactly what Law E produces.** Ten
casts at full life spend **0** — `sub_56270`'s `actLife < maxLife` leg
refuses, the `else` arm forces `+48 = 1` (:65120) and the shared
`--(+48)` zeroes it, so the burst releases BEFORE `sub_55E80` is
reached and nothing touches the regen delta. The exchange rate on zero
health owed is zero. Pinned by
`heal_at_full_life_is_free_however_many_times_it_is_cast`
(reversion-probed).

**Second half: MEASURED NOT TO HAPPEN, and the decompile says it
cannot.** The release is TERMINAL, not a pause: a refused tick ends the
burst, so damage taken afterwards finds no counter to restart. Probe —
burst heals 9,605 → 10,000 and pays 1,000 on its first tick, `+48`
drops 20 → 0 on the second (life now full), and 3,000 damage after
that produces only passive regen (5/tick, no mana). Retail has no arm
that can resurrect a zeroed `+48`. ⭐ From the player's seat the two
readings are indistinguishable, which is presumably why the guess felt
right: **a full-life cast is free and dies instantly, and the next cast
while hurt pays in full** — "it starts costing again when I'm hurt" is
the re-cast, not a resumption.

⚠ **THE MC2 HALF OF THE OBSERVATION IS UNMET FOR A DIFFERENT REASON —
THE HUMAN'S MC2 HEAL DOES NOT HEAL AT ALL.** `mc2/cast.rs` spell 5 sets
`player.heal_active = true` at the cast (EF:56432) and the expiry arm
clears it (:1688), and **nothing reads it**: an exhaustive sweep of

have a channel (`mc2/rivals.rs` :1476, rate approximated as

column has none. MC2 also debits at the manifestation tick
(`sub_68DE0`, the `sub_55E80` twin), so whether MC2's heal carries the
same `actLife < maxLife` admission is a separate read that has not been
done. **Named as a dig, not fixed here** — no certified MC2 take casts
heal, so it is unwitnessed and landing it blind would be a
reconstruction.

### RULES THIS SESSION PROVED

- ⭐⭐⭐ **A LAW LANDED ON ONE CALL PATH IS NOT LANDED.** Three of five:
  the ctor-vs-cast extents, Shield's token body, Heal's token body.
  The strict/native token-encoding split is a standing trap — every
  spell body wired into the `strict_retail` walk needs the
  `manifestation_tick` twin checked at the same time.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **A MISATTRIBUTED LAW HIDES AS A HOLE ON ITS OTHER CONSUMER.**
  The extents doubling looked landed for a whole campaign because its
  one witnessed consumer (the possess lob) read correctly; the magnet,
  which shares the ctor and has no cast arm, silently ran at half size.
  When a law is attributed to a call site, ask what ELSE reaches the
  cited line.
- ⭐⭐ **`--limit N` ON verify-deltas COUNTS PAIRS FROM THE START, SO
  `--dump T --limit 1` GRADES PAIR 0, NOT PAIR T.** A "1 conforming"
  verdict from that combination is about the first tick of the take and
  says nothing about T. It nearly cost the session two pair fixtures
  (both heads read as pair-blind, both were pair-visible).
- ⭐⭐ **THE RAW-SHADOW CENSUS OVER A FREE RUN NAMED FOUR OF THE FIVE
  HEADS BY ITSELF.** Every one of these was a clean-`D1(t)` break, and
  the first tick a lane parts (`(9,17) f80 … t=2723`, `(9,1) f80 …
  360 vs 180`) is the whole diagnosis.
- ⚙ Probe discipline held: `git diff -- crates/ > laws.patch` BEFORE
  writing the unit pins, `git apply -R`, rebuild, run — all four pins
  and both new fixtures failed on their own lanes, no other fixture
  moved — then `git apply` and `git apply -R --check` to prove the
  restoration bit-identical.

## SESSION 72 — THE GALORES OPEN: RETAIL'S BOLT PARKS, DROWNS, AND BILLS NOTHING

The focus set moved to the three spell-galore takes (charter amendment,
player-ratified at session 71 close): every divergence in a take that
deliberately exercises every spell is a MECHANIC gap, so the grind
converts straight into feature correctness. Two takes ridden in
parallel — `mc1l0-spells-galore` (the shortest road to END in the
corpus) and `mc2l6-rival-spells-galore` (the smallest horizon head) —
with `mc2l0-spells-galore` held per session 71's inherited-head ruling.

**Seven laws landed. mc1l0-sg 1,618 -> 2,732 (+1,114); mc2l6 69 -> 70
with clean ticks 135 -> 268. Certified 12/12 END devs=0.**

### THE CLUSTER CENSUS — WHY THE GALORES ARE WORTH RIDING

`replay --segmented --classify` over all three takes first, then the
heads clustered by signature. `mc1l0-spells-galore` returns **277 heads,
276 of them LOCAL** (a one-tick law each, no inherited debt anywhere in
the take) collapsing into just EIGHT shapes — 243 on the human's `mana`
alone, 24 on a `(10,55)` the port never spawns, and the rest in ones and
twos. That concentration is the galore doctrine paying out: a take built
to exercise every spell puts every mechanic gap in its own tight cluster.

`mc2l6-rival-spells-galore` is the opposite shape — 39,574 excess resets
in 77 runs, desyncing hard from t~309 — so only its first four heads are
tractable and everything past them is downstream noise.

### LAW A — THE PAYLOAD STRIKE PARKS ON THE VICTIM'S AIM POINT (mc1/combat.rs)

`sub_52770`'s victim arm (:62751-55, CARPET.EXE 0x52d42) is
`sub_524C0(victim); sub_41C70(bolt, victim+72); sub_524E0(victim)` — the
`+76/+78` lift bracket (:62503-22, the only such pair in the image),
so the bolt teleports to `(victim.x, victim.y, victim.z + victim.f78)`
and the explode mints the child THERE. It is NOT a tile snap; buildings
simply sit on tile centres. The arithmetic closes to the unit at two
independent heads against two different buildings:

    t=1619  building slot 6:    544 + (-8192) = -7648   x/y 16640/13312
    t=1724  building slot 651: 1280 + (-8192) = -6912   x/y 13312/12032

Retail's whole no-victim block is one bracket; a strike tick never

### LAW C — THE PAYLOAD LOB DROWNS (mc1/combat.rs)

The class-9 water arm (:62690-701, CARPET 0x52a44-0x52a7a) was missing
from the payload path though `proj_move_and_hit` and `proj_m8_tick`

## SESSION 83 — THE WRAPPER, THE CREDIT, THE HALF-TURN AND THE RAW RESPAWN (mc2l6-rsg 2031 → 3368)

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore`
CERTIFIED and held at END; **`mc2l6-rival-spells-galore` 2031 → 3368**;
`mc2l0-spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). FIVE laws off one head
chain — 2032 → 2165 → 2547 → 3084 → 3258 — and every one of them was a
CONTROL-FLOW shape the port had paraphrased: a switch that reads a
field the caller just wrote, a subtraction with an invented floor, a
loop whose first statement had migrated to the end, a function whose
two callers share a body the port had split in half, and a dispatch
order the port had frozen into a constant. The fifth is the fourth's
own consequence — landing law D moved a respawned wizard's book below
it and made a slot relationship the port had hard-coded stop holding.

### ⭐⭐⭐ RULES THIS SESSION PROVED

- **⭐⭐⭐ AN INVENTED GUARD IS FALSE EXACTLY WHEN IT MATTERS.** Three
  of the four laws are a predicate retail does not have. The phase-7
  wrapper's `actionIndex & 7 == 7` re-test is true on every quiet tick
  and false on the ONE tick per hold that the wrapper exists to
  handle. The duel drain's `max(0)` on the regen term is a no-op on
  every ordinary tick and wrong on exactly the ticks the victim is
  casting. A guard that "obviously cannot matter" is a guard nobody
  measured — and both of these were sitting in front of graded lanes
  for months.
- **⭐⭐⭐ READ THE LOOP'S FIRST STATEMENT, NOT ITS BODY.** `sub_35640`
  seeds a yaw and then OPENS its do-while with the half-turn, so the
  storm's first beam already carries it. A `base + k * 1024` loop
  produces the same PAIR of beams and is wrong about which one is
  spawned first — and since the pair is symmetric, no arithmetic
  assertion about the two beams can tell the two versions apart. Only
  the register the loop leaves on the CLOUD can. ⭐ WHEN AN ORDERING
  BUG PRODUCES A SYMMETRIC SET, PIN THE EMITTER'S OWN STATE.
- **⭐⭐⭐ A SHARED CTOR/REUSE FUNCTION IS A LAW ABOUT WHAT THE REUSE
  ARM DOES *NOT* DO.** `sub_5C950` is one function for minting a
  wizard and for respawning one, and the entire per-map difficulty
  block — Aggression, Perception, Reflexes and the Life scalar that
  divides maxLife — lives inside the NEW-ENTITY arm. So a respawned
  MC2 rival comes back at the RAW 10000 maxLife and 256 Life scalar:
  a rival authored at Life 51 returns from its first death five times
  the wizard it was. The port had reimplemented the reuse arm from
  scratch and re-filled the OLD ceilings.
- **⭐⭐ THE SIGN OF A MIS-ORDERED PAIR IS THAT THE TWO RECORDS HOLD
  EACH OTHER'S VALUES, LANE FOR LANE — nothing is missing, nothing is
  extra, and the free stacks agree at both ends. mc2l6-rsg t=2547
  looked like a mass-spawn desync and was one line of control flow.
- **⭐⭐ A FIXTURE THAT FAILS ON SOMEBODY ELSE'S LAW IS A MAP OF THE
  BLINDNESS.** The law-A pair at t=2031 cut cleanly and then failed on
  `(3,1) mana` — rival 370's duel drain, which the take's own
  verify-deltas sweep grades CLEAN at that tick because the sweep's
  carried World still holds a duel lock the 3-record fixture cannot.
  ⚠ THE SWEEP'S WORLD IS ITS OWN STATE CHANNEL: "the pair is clean at
  t" and "a fixture cut at t passes" are different claims.
- **⚠ A RE-MINT THAT CHECKS WHETHER THE OLD ONE IS STILL ALIVE IS A
  PORT INVENTION.** `sub_5CF40` overwrites `SpellEnabled[i]` with a
  brand-new class-15 for every known spell and simply ORPHANS whatever
  was there — which is coherent only because SESSION 82's law C had
  already established that the death scatter never frees those tokens.
- **⭐⭐⭐ A LAW THAT MOVES ENTITIES BETWEEN SLOTS INVALIDATES EVERY
  COMMENT THAT ASSUMED THE OLD ORDER.** Law E was law D's own
  consequence, and the port had written the assumption down verbatim
  — *"the token's own pool slot sits ABOVE the wizard's … so the
  class-15 handler runs LATER IN THAT SAME FRAME"* — as the
  justification for emulating the token body at the caster's slot.
  Law D put a respawned book BELOW its wizard and the justification
  silently stopped holding. ⭐ AFTER LANDING AN ALLOCATION LAW, GREP
  THE TREE FOR COMMENTS THAT REASON ABOUT SLOT ORDER.
- **⭐⭐ WHEN A "MISSING/EXTRA" SIGNATURE NAMES A SPAWNER, CHECK
  WHETHER THE SPAWNER RAN BEFORE BLAMING ITS GATE.** t=3258's extra
  (10,2) read as a speed-sustain refusal; the free stack settled it in
  one call — retail popped ONE slot where the port popped TWO, so
  nothing was over-spawning the puff and something else was spawning

port makes that retail does not.** Session 83 found invented

### LAW A — the reuse arm's zero-writes are an ENUMERATED LIST, and the combat FSMs are not on it

`sub_5C950` (EF:43694-43843) writes, in the reuse arm: `word_0x159_345`,
`word_0x24C_588`, `dword_0x16D_365`, `speed_0xc_12`, `yaw_0x1E_30`,
`fov_0x22_34`, `moveBoost_0x1E_30`, `strafeSpeed_0x10_16`, an 18-byte
`memset(&str_0x1AC_428, 0, 18)`, `word_0x24A_586`, `word_0x146_326` /
`word_0x148_328`, and — only under `model_0x40_64 == 1` — the brain
byte `byte_0x1C1_449`, the eight hate words and `SpellEnabled[2]`.

Four of the port's zero-writes are not on that list, and the offsets
say why:

- the burst counter `word_0x1A2_418` and the poverty latch
  `word_0x1A4_420` sit **BELOW** the memset's 0x1AC..0x1BD window;
- the weave FSM (`str_611` 0x45D) and its committed direction
  (0x45C), and the water-steer FSM (0x45E/0x45F), live in `str_611`,
  which the reuse arm never touches;
- the target `word_0x96_150` is an **ENTITY** field — the reuse arm
  keeps the entity and never re-enters it (the NEW-entity arm gets a
  fresh, zeroed record from `IfSubtypeCallCreatingManaSphere_4A190`,
  which is why the mint looks like it clears them).

The recording says it outright. Rival 378's player block across its
respawn at t=3084:

```
t=3083  ai_state=11 burst=2 charge=6 invuln=0   cmd_speed=80 weave=1/8 cd=[(1,3)]
t=3084  ai_state=0  burst=2 charge=6 invuln=100 cmd_speed=0  weave=1/8 cd=[(1,3),(2,8)]
```

Only `ai_state`, `invuln`, `cmd_speed` and `cooldown[2]` move —
`burst`, `charge`, `weave`, `weave_dir` and `brake` all ride through
death untouched.

**`weave` is the one that bites.** The weave FSM's tick-0 arm is the
only arm that *does* anything: it draws the ENTITY LCG, rolls a
committed direction and snaps the actual yaw ±512; ticks 3..19 only
coast. So a respawned rival that retail leaves at `weave` 8 —
coasting — was, in the port, re-rolling a fresh jink, spending a draw
nothing else spends and steering off. That debt rode 285 ungraded
ticks before it surfaced as the wizard's own `z`/`pitch` at t=3369.
**+151.**

`mc2_rival_respawn`, mc2/rivals.rs.

### LAW B — the at-castle grace pin is an ASSIGNMENT, not a floor

`sub_12A70` initialises `v2 = 0` (EF:5356), raises it only on the
castle-overlap test, and then does `if (v2) word_0x159_345 = 2`
(EF:5398-99). So docking does not merely *keep* a wizard's grace
alive — it **CLOBBERS a larger one down to 2**, and the very next
statement's `--` parks it at 1 for as long as the wizard stays home.

It matters exactly once per life, and it is the tick a rival
respawns: `sub_5C950` re-anchors it AT ITS OWN CASTLE with
`word_0x159_345 = 100` (session 83 law D), so the first `sub_12A70`
after the respawn throws 98 ticks of that grace away. Rival 378
respawns at t=3084 with 100 and the recording reads **1** from t=3085
on; the port's `.max(2)` kept the whole 100.

The consequence is bigger than the counter. Retail's structure is
`if (word_0x159_345) { memset(&str_0x5E_94, 0, 36); word_0x159_345--; }
else if (sub_5EFA0(a1x) == 2) {...}` — and `sub_5EFA0`'s FIRST
statement is `a1x->word_0x26_38 = 0`. So a wizard that never leaves
the grace branch never re-zeroes its attacker latch. The port sat in
that branch for 99 ticks it had no business being immune for, and
when it finally ran the intake it latched a letter retail had already
eaten — leaving `word_0x26_38` stale at 343 for **400 ticks**.

Horizon-neutral, strongly non-vacuous: the census `wiz 2 invuln` row
(107 rows t=83..3183) went to **zero**, and `(3,1) f26` collapsed from
**56 rows to 1**.

⭐ **The MC2 HUMAN column has had the plain assignment all along**
(`world.rs`, the `grace = 2` beside the same memset). Session 82's
standing lesson once more: the rival column missing what another
column of this same port already had right.

`mc2_rival_alive`, mc2/rivals.rs.

## SESSION 86 — THE CASTLE OWNER IS NOT ONLY THE HUMAN (mc2l6-rsg 4309 → 4493)

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore` held
CERTIFIED at END; **mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 4309 → 4493 (+184)**;
`mc2l0-spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). FIVE laws off ONE head
chain (4310 → 4312 → 4477), each landing exposing the next.

Session 83 found invented PREDICATES, 84 invented ASSIGNMENTS, 85 the
possession workers doing what no other worker does. **86 is a
PRONOUN**: four of the five laws are the port reading "the human"
where retail wrote "the castle's owner", "the setpoint" where retail
wrote "the actual", or "every candidate" where retail wrote "the
election winner". The fifth is a decompile TYPE that the shipped
binary contradicts.

### The rules this session proved

- **⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIPPED EXE OUTRANKS THE LISTING — AND A DECLARED TYPE
  IS PART OF THE LISTING.** remc2's `axis_3d` declares `x`/`y` as
  `uint16_t`, so every `a2->x - a1->x` in a distance helper promotes
  to `int` and cannot wrap. `NETHERW.EXE` @0x2393B0 disassembles to
  `mov ax,[ecx] / sub ax,[esi] / cwde / cdq / xor eax,edx / sub
  eax,edx` per axis: a **16-bit** subtraction, SIGN-EXTENDED, then
  `abs`. The whole law lives in one `cwde` that a header file erased.
  When a numeric law refuses to reproduce, disassemble the helper
  before re-reading its callers.
- **⭐⭐⭐ RETAIL GATES THE ELECTION WINNER, NOT THE CANDIDATES —
  FOURTH SIGHTING, AND THIS ONE ELECTS BY A DIFFERENT METRIC THAN IT
  GATES BY.** `sub_13B00` ranks foreign castles by
  `EuclideanDistXY_584D0` inside `sub_14B10` and hands only the winner
  to `sub_583B0`. A port `min` over one metric is not the same
  question, and no amount of re-reading the gate finds it.
- **⭐⭐⭐ "HUMAN ONLY" IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE PORT, NOT ABOUT RETAIL.**
  Three of this session's five laws were one early return
  (`if own != PLAYER_TARGET { return }`) or one hardcoded lookup
  (`self.mc2_book`) standing where retail indexes
  `Entities_EA3E4[castle->id_0x1A_26]->…->SpellsEnabled[2]`. Grep the
  port for `PLAYER_TARGET` guards on paths whose retail body takes an
  entity pointer.
- **⭐⭐ A PORT COMMENT THAT EXPLAINS WHY A LAW IS INERT IS A STANDING
  HEAD — FOURTH SESSION RUNNING.** `mc2_castle_lock_stamp` carried
  "⚠ HUMAN ONLY … MC2 rivals cast through `mc2_rival_cast_castle`,
  which owns no class-15 record for the stamp to land on. Unported,
  and inert." The per-rival `Mc2Spellbook` has carried `book.ent[2]`
  all along, and two other functions in the same file read its tier.
  (cf. 81's "cannot be landed", 84's `.max()`, 85's "not in the
  current corpus".)
- **⭐⭐ THE MODEL BYTE IS NOT THE ROLE.** `sub_605E0`'s level-0 arm
  branches on the castle owner's `model_0x40_64 == 1`, which reads as
  "a wizard" — but mc2l6-rsg's own pool says the HUMAN's carpet is
  class-3 model **0** and only rivals 370/378/383 are model 1. Reading
  it as "a wizard" would have changed the human column for no reason;
  reading the corpus made the law human-neutral. **Resolve a model
  test against the recording's pool, never against the name.**
- **⚠⚠ "THE PAIR IS CLEAN AT THE HORIZON" DOES NOT MEAN A FIXTURE
  CUTS THERE.** The t=4309 pair carries a standing unrelated residue —
  the rival damage MAILBOX has no import seat, so slot 383 imports
  life 2926 against retail's 2726 — and the cut fixture failed on
  `field:3,1:life`. It was deleted rather than kept, and law A rides
  law B's unit pin instead.

### The laws

- **A — THE LADDER RE-SYNC RE-PRICES THE CASTLE OWNER'S OWN
  CREATE-CASTLE TOKEN.** `sub_60810`'s `locEvent2` (EF:61697-61701) is
  `Entities_EA3E4[castle->id_0x1A_26]->dword_0xA4_164x->str_611
  .SpellsEnabled[2]` — no player test — and `sub_60780` (EF:61670-83)

## SESSION 85 — POSSESSION IS THE ODD ONE OUT (mc2l6-rsg 3519 → 4309)

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore` held
CERTIFIED at END; **mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 3519 → 4309 (+790)**;
`mc2l0-spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). SIX laws.

Five of the six are the POSSESSION spell, and they share one shape:
**the two possession workers do what no other impact worker does, or
skip what all of them do.** The galore doctrine paid again — the take
exercises the spell deliberately, so every divergence in the chain was
a mechanic gap, not a numeric one.

### ⭐⭐⭐ Rules this session proved

- **⭐⭐⭐ A CALL SITE LIST IS AN ENUMERATED LIST.** `sub_686D0` is
  called from four places and the port folded ALL impacts into one
  seam that called it unconditionally. `grep` for the helper, not for
  the callers you expect — the two possession workers are missing from
  the list and that absence IS the law. Same shape as session 84's
  reset-function writes.
- **⭐⭐⭐ A CTOR'S HARDCODED MODEL OUTRANKS THE SUBTYPE THAT SELECTED
  IT.** `_4A190(&pos, 10, 69)` resolves to `AddAuxiliary_50500`, whose
  third statement is `model_0x40_64 = 0x36`. The port assumed the
  spawn pair it passed IN was the pair that came OUT.
- **⭐⭐⭐ SOFT KILL IS NOT A FREE — AGAIN, ON A NEW LOOP.** The ball
  tick's collector test already carried this law; the magnet's scan
  did not. When a corpus law is "retail's loop has no 0x400 test",
  audit every OTHER loop over the same chain.
- **⭐⭐ A PORT COMMENT THAT SAYS "not in the current corpus" IS A
  STANDING HEAD.** Law F's whole mechanism was written down in
  `mc2_manifestation_tick` as an untraced approximation; the galore
  take put it in the corpus and the decompile block was five lines.
- **⭐⭐ WHEN A CADENCE GATE AND A PER-TICK HANDLER SHARE A TARGET
  REGISTER, ASK WHO ELSE WRITES IT.** Rival 378's ball pick runs every
  52 ticks; its possess cast runs every tick. One spurious write to
  `word_0x96_150` between two picks costs the whole goal, because
  `sub_14C60` compares a SIGNATURE that the fresh victim will not
  match.
- **⚠ AN OBS CHANNEL WITHOUT A LANE CANNOT ASSERT A LAW.**
  `word_0x96_150` is absent from the `.mgcr` entity record, so law A's
  pair fixture passed under the reverted build. It was DELETED, not
  kept. Measure before you cut.

## SESSION 88 — WHOSE SLOT STAMPED IT, AND WHICH ARM DREW (mc2l6-rsg 4847 → 6290)

Focus = the galores (standing player ask). `mc1l0-spells-galore` held
CERTIFIED at END; **mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 4847 → 6290 (+1443)** on
FOUR laws off one head chain (4848 → 5291 → 5565 → 6269); `mc2l0-
spells-galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). Every other row in the
25-row board byte-held.

83 invented PREDICATES · 84 invented ASSIGNMENTS · 85 the possession
workers as the odd ones out · 86 a PRONOUN · 87 a predicate that was a
WRITE. **88 is PHASE and PLACEMENT**: three of the four laws are not
about *what* the port computes but about *whose walk slot stamped the
value*, *which arm of an if the draw lives in*, and *which of 26
otherwise-identical handlers puts its call one brace deeper*.

### ⭐⭐⭐ RULES THIS SESSION PROVED

- **⭐⭐⭐ A FLAG A TOKEN RE-STAMPS EVERY TICK IS NOT A BOOLEAN THE
  CAST LATCHES.** `sub_6AA00` writes the owner's window bit at the
  TOKEN's own walk slot, and the consumer reads it live off the
  victim's record at the PROJECTILE's slot. Deriving it once at the
  tick head is right on every tick but the arm frame — and the arm
  frame is exactly when a bolt is already in flight at you.
- **⭐⭐⭐ WHICH ARM OF AN IF THE RNG DRAW LIVES IN IS A LAW.** The
  port hoisted `rand = 9377*rand + 9439` above `if (precise)`, where
  retail has it inside the `else`. Every precise deflection then rode
  a stream one step out of phase for the rest of the bolt's life. A
  hoist looks like a refactor and is not.
- **⭐⭐⭐ TWENTY-SIX HANDLERS THAT LOOK LIKE ONE SKELETON ARE NOT ONE
  SKELETON.** `sub_68DE0`'s placement inside each manifestation body
  is hand-written, and six of the twenty-six nest it INSIDE the
  first-tick block. Diff the handlers; do not infer the skeleton.
  (Same family as 84/85: **a call-site list is an ENUMERATED LIST**.)
- **⭐⭐⭐ GREP THE OTHER COLUMN FIRST — SIXTH SESSION RUNNING.** Law A
  is MC1's `world.rs` spell-14 mid-walk republish, verbatim, and its
  own doc comment already cited the mc1hwl0 t=38740 witness.
- **⭐⭐ A "🏦 CANNOT BE ASSERTED YET" NOTE CAN BE WRONG ABOUT THE
  CLAIM, NOT JUST THE WITNESS.** Session 87 banked the rebound pitch
  flip as "not a negate" (53 → 1984 where a negate gives 1995). With
  the helpers read out (`sub_582F0`/`sub_582B0`, Sound.cpp:6569/6580 —
  the SIGN and the MAGNITUDE of the shortest turn from 0), the product
  is `pitch` folded into (−1024, 1024] and the store is `(−pitch) &
  0x7FF` for EVERY input. The note had sampled the pitch one statement
  too early — before `sub_65610`'s steer leg. **CLOSED as a non-law**;
  the real miss beside it was that retail writes `fov_0x22_34` as well
  as `pitch_0x1E_30`, which the port never did.
- **⚠⚠ A VACUOUS UNIT PIN CAN LOOK LIKE A GOOD ONE.** The roster-chain
  pin's first shape ran a lap to build the chains — and the
  action-0xE8 creature DESPAWNS ITSELF in that lap, so the reverted
  pool walk skipped it for a different reason and the probe passed.
  Setting the roster by hand (the builder is pinned elsewhere) made
  the pin assert the picker and nothing else.

- **A — THE REBOUND WINDOW IS STAMPED AT THE TOKEN'S OWN WALK SLOT**

  the tier's own bit off `SPELLS[model].subspell[b46].life_0x1A` — 0 →
  `byte[1] |= 0x80` (scatter), 1 → `byte[0] |= 0x10` (precise), and

## SESSION 87 — THE PREDICATE THAT WAS A WRITE (mc2l6-rsg 4493 → 4847)

Focus = the galores. `mc1l0-spells-galore` held CERTIFIED at END;
**mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 4493 → 4847 (+354)** on THREE law
families off one head chain (4494 → 4559 → 4567); `mc2l0-spells-
galore` HELD at 8,103 (untouched). Every other row in the 17-take
sweep byte-held.

83 found invented PREDICATES, 84 invented ASSIGNMENTS, 85 the
possession workers as the odd ones out, 86 a PRONOUN. **87 is a
predicate that was a WRITE** — twice over, plus a constant that was a
parameter.

### ⭐⭐⭐ RULES THIS SESSION PROVED

- **⭐⭐⭐ A GUARD AND A CLEAR ARE NOT THE SAME LAW, EVEN WHEN THEY
  TEST THE SAME THING.** `sub_14C60` asks only "is this still the same
  record?"; `sub_5EFA0` asks "is it dead?" and, if so, ERASES the
  pointer. Folding the second into the first looks like a refactor and
  is not: the clear is reachable only on a NOT-DOCKED tick, so the two
  disagree for the whole length of a wizard's castle grace, and they
  disagree in the direction that costs a whole handler body. **When a
  port expresses a stateful invalidation as a stateless predicate, ask
  what gates the write.**
- **⭐⭐⭐ A CONSTANT IN THE PORT WHERE RETAIL HAS A PARAMETER IS A
  SILENT ONE-CALL-PATH LAW.** `sub_68740(a1x, a2x, a3, a4)` takes its
  scatter window from the caller, and four of five callers agree — so
  the port's hardcoded 0x2D/22 tested fine everywhere except the one
  body that flies a plain fireball. **Grep a helper's call sites for
  DISAGREEING literal arguments before porting it with the majority
  value.** (cf. session 85's enumerated call-site list.)
- **⭐⭐⭐ "DELIBERATE APPROXIMATION" IS A CLAIM WITH AN EXPIRY DATE —
  AND THE SEAT MAY ALREADY EXIST.** `mc2_rebound_deflect` carried "the
  human's mana debit is skipped (the wizard ledger is world-side)"
  while `Gen::player_deflect_debit` — built, hashed, and drained at
  BOTH the pre- and post-carpet drains — had been sitting there for
  the MC1 column's twin law. FIFTH session running that a port comment
  explaining an inertness was the standing head. (cf. 81 "cannot be
  landed", 84 `.max()`, 85 "not in the current corpus", 86 "HUMAN
  ONLY … inert".)
- **⭐⭐⭐ GREP THE OTHER COLUMN FIRST — AGAIN, AND FOR THE *SEAT* NOT
  JUST THE SYMBOL.** Two of the three families were already right on
  the MC1 column: `watcom_rand` at the anti-rebound roll, and the
  deflect debit's whole plumbing.
- **⚠⚠ A HEAD AT t ANCHORS ITS FIXTURE AT t−1 — AND THE PROBE IS THE
  ONLY THING THAT PROVES IT.** The anti-rebound fixture was cut at
  t=4557 for a head at 4559, passed the suite, and was VACUOUS. Only
  the reversion probe caught it. It was deleted rather than kept as
  ballast, and the law went to a unit pin.
- **⚠⚠ A "REVERT EVERYTHING RETAIL DOESN'T HAVE" SWEEP CAN MEASURE
  MUCH WORSE.** Dropping the port's reap proxy (`flags & 0x400`) along
  with the invented life test took the horizon 4493 → **965**. The
  proxy stands in for a reap→free timing the port does not share with
  retail. Isolate invented predicates ONE AT A TIME; the decompile
  says both are absent, and the corpus says only one of them is.

### THE LAWS

- **A — THE GATE IS A PURE SIGNATURE COMPARE.** `sub_14C60` (EF:6707)
  = `sub_14C40(a2x) == a1x->word_0x98_152` = `id + model +
  (class << 7)`, and the six handlers that open with it — `sub_12FF0`
  :5586, `sub_131F0` :5664, `sub_135C0` :5831, `sub_13710` :5880,
  `sub_13890` :5953, `sub_161A0` :7744 — test nothing else. Freeing a
  record clears `class_0x3F_63`, so the free IS the invalidation.
  Port: `mc2_target_alive` loses `act_life >= 0` (the reap proxy
  stays, see above).
- **B — THE DEAD-TARGET CLEAR IS `sub_5EFA0`'s SECOND BLOCK**
  (EF:60634-39), reachable only via `sub_12A70`'s
  `word_0x159_345 == 0` arm (EF:5400-19). Ported to the top of
  `mc2_rival_intake`. t=4494/4495 pin the two sides of the grace
  edge. **A+B = +65.** Two pair fixtures, each failing only under its
  own revert.
- **C — THE ANTI-REBOUND ROLL IS `watcomrand()`** (EF:7212), not the
  entity LCG. **+8.** Unit pin (`mc2_anti_rebound_roll_leaves_the_
  rivals_entity_lcg_alone`).
- **D — `sub_68740` ON FOUR COUNTS**: the scatter window is the call
  site's `(a3, a4)` and `sub_65C20` alone passes `(0x5B, 45)`
  (EF:63162); the victim's mana/4 gate AND debit apply to the human
  (EF:55232/55284); the landing is `victim.z + array_0x52_82.fov`
  (EF:55302-04), the quad's FOURTH word; the collide pair re-keys off
  the old shooter's class/model for any shooter (EF:55298-300).
  **+281.** Unit pins in `mc2_rebound_deflects_and_reowns`, each
  probed. The scatter half also corrected that test's own ±22
  assertion.

  neighbours a quarter-tile away, and its missing radius counted
  tile-mates half a map-height below. Only one head shows each way,
  and they were consecutive. **When a port reduces a ring-plus-radius

## SESSION 94 (2026-09-03) — THE INDEX SPACE, THE ROW THE ALLOCATOR SEEDS, AND A TOOL THAT WAS 5x SLOWER THAN THE WORK

Session 93 banked the MC2 allocator row seed WITH A BLOCKER: landing it
panicked `the_mc2_hate_ledger_is_the_tick_top_projectile_sweep`, because
`row156` was being carried in two different index spaces at once. This
session opened by auditing that convention. The audit WAS the landing.

**mc2l6-rival-spells-galore 10,087 → 10,109, clean 10,319 → 11,339**
(the seed +22/+343, the (10,57) merge law a further +677 clean).
**mc2l22 412 HELD.**

### ⭐⭐⭐ EACH ALLOCATOR SEEDS ITS OWN TABLE'S BASE ROW

Retail carries a POINTER (`dword_0xA0_160x` on MC2,
`var_u32_29951_156` on MC1), so every read is absolute by construction
and the index-space question never arises there. The port carries a
`u8` INDEX, so it has to be stated — and it is different per column:

- **MC1 — `unk_98F38`, 0-based.** `NewEvent_372C0` writes
  `var_u32_29951_156 = unk_98F38` (sub_main.cpp:43877 free pop, :43902
  sacrifice) — the table BASE, which IS index 0.
- **MC2 — `str_D7BD6`, ABSOLUTE, base 59.** `NewEvent_4A050` writes
  `dword_0xA0_160x = &str_D7BD6[59]` in BOTH arms (Events.cpp:573,
  :599).

⇒ **Both allocators seed the base row; the base is a different NUMBER
on each column.** `Ent::default()` already served MC1 for free, which is
exactly why the omission on MC2 stayed invisible for so long. Every
natively spawned MC2 record had been running `BEHAVIOR[0]` — the (5,0)
creature row, hover band `v_12 = 7` and drift `v_14 = +244` — instead
of row 59's `0` / `−4`. Wrong floor, wrong vertical drift, on
everything the sim mints.

### THE CONVENTION AUDIT (the blocker itself)

`row156` is now **ABSOLUTE on the MC2 column, with no exceptions**.
Three sites disagreed, and each was its own small law:

- **The (3,3) balloon was the one RELATIVE holdout.** `mc2_spawn_balloon`
  stamped 9 and `mc2_balloon_tick` read `BEHAVIOR[ROW_BASE + row156]`,
  self-consistent but off-convention — and it had forced a matching
  EXCEPTION into `import_ent_mc2`, which subtracted `ROW_BASE` for
  class 3 model 3 alone. Both sides are absolute now (the ctor
  `sub_4ABA0` pins `&str_D7BD6[68]`, EF:33422) and the importer
  exception is deleted. Behaviourally a no-op by construction
  (`ROW_BASE + 9 == 68`), except that the old `saturating_sub` clamped
  any imported balloon row below 59 to the base instead of its own row.
- **The two MC2 cave arms double-offset an absolute index.**
  `ball_tick`'s cave fan and `mc2_fool_flight` (mc1/combat.rs) read
  `BEHAVIOR[ROW_BASE + row156]` where retail's `sub_11E70`
  (Terrain.cpp:2152) reads the entity's OWN row pointer,
  `event->dword_0xA0_160x->word_160_0xc_12`. With MC2 projectile rows
  at 60-65 that indexed rows 119-124, and anything above row 97 would
  have panicked outright. ⚠ A/B-EXCLUDED on the cave golden: fixing
  them moves NOTHING there even though it IS a caves world.
- ⭐⭐ **A SHARED HANDLER MUST READ THE CALLER'S TABLE, NOT ITS OWN
  FILE'S.** `Gen::home` (mc1/combat.rs:1498) is MC1's `sub_52550` and
  `BEHAVIOR` resolves to MC1's 31-row table inside that file — but MC2
  class-9 records reach it. That was a silent wrong-row read for as
  long as MC2 rows happened to be 0, and an index-out-of-bounds panic
  the moment the allocator seeded 59. It now selects the table off
  `verbs.movement`. **This is the whole blocker: the seed did not break
  anything, it EXPOSED something.** (Both columns' homers are the same
  4-argument primitive — MC1 `sub_422A0(cur, want, v_4, v_2)` at
  sub_main.cpp:62547, MC2 `sub_58350` at EF:58597 — so the shared body
  is the right shape; only the table lookup was wrong.)

### ⭐ THE MANA SPHERE'S INVENTED ROLL — 88,290 CENSUS ROWS, ONE LINE

`TransformEntityToManaSphere_36BA0` (EF:26903) writes
`yaw_0x1C_28` and NOTHING else on each scattered sphere; the port also
stamped `roll_0x20_32` (our `f34`) with the same value. The pairing of
yaw and roll IS a real MC2 idiom — the cave fan does exactly that
(EF:26221-22, `roll_0x20_32 = v31; yaw_0x1C_28 = v31`) — which is
presumably how it migrated here. It does not belong to the scatter.
A/B-ATTRIBUTED on the cave golden: this one line moves checkpoint D and
leaves A/B/C byte-identical.

### ⚠ THE SEED HAS NO FIXTURE HOME — AND THE DIG PROVED IT

The pair lane re-imports `row156` from the recording on EVERY pair
(`import_ent_mc2` decodes `ptr_a0` through retail's own
`(ptr − base160)/34 + 59` fixup, Level.cpp:1255-57), so a natively
seeded row NEVER FIRES there. Measured independently by the parallel
(10,57) dig: the whole-take `verify-deltas --csv` census on
mc2l6-rival-spells-galore is **byte-identical across the landing** —
48,268 rows before and after, every family unchanged. The law pays in
FREE RUN only. It is therefore guarded by a UNIT TEST
(`each_allocator_seeds_its_own_behavior_table_base`, docs/CONFORMANCE.md
§Lifecycle 4), proven non-vacuous by reverting the seed.

⭐ That census is also the cleanest possible statement that the landing
regressed nothing on the pair lane of the focus take — a shape worth
reusing: **ask a dig already holding a whole-take census to re-run it
across your landing.**

### ⭐⭐⭐ THE FOOL'S (10,57) SPHERE MERGES — AND THE MEMBERSHIP TEST IS A PARAMETER, NOT A CONSTANT

A parallel dig went after the banked "(10,57) late band, 2,455 z rows"
and **refuted it outright** — that was session 93's START census; the
family is 657 rows today and only 51 of them are `z`. The real law was
three subsystems away and is one of the better ones this campaign has
found.

Retail's m57 tick `sub_35FB0` reaches the SAME partner search the ball
does and ends in **`sub_36F30`, not `sub_36D50`** — a different
function, not a variant — and there is **no `byte[1] & 0x20` decay test
in front of it**: the ball's decay gate (EF:26268) is the BALL's alone,
so a DECAYING fool's sphere still absorbs. The port early-returned on
`is_fool` and never merged m57 at all.

And the partner filter is not a constant. **`sub_10A50` matches the
SEEKER's OWN `xtype`/`xsubtype` (@0x41/@0x42) against the candidate's
class/model (@0x3f/@0x40), with −1 a wildcard on either half.**
Re-verified here from the shipped EXE at file 0x352d9-0x35301:

    movsbl 0x41(%esi),%eax ; cmp $-1,%eax ; je accept
    mov    0x41(%esi),%al  ; cmp 0x3f(%ebx),%al ; jne …
    movsbl 0x42(%esi),%eax ; cmp $-1,%eax ; je accept
    mov    0x41(%esi),%al  ; cmp 0x3f(%ebx),%al ; jne reject
    mov    0x42(%esi),%al  ; cmp 0x40(%ebx),%al ; jne reject

…and `sub_50130` stamps that pair as **(10, 57)**, not the shared
ctor's (10, 39) — file 0x7494f `movb $0xa,0x41(%eax)` / 0x74953
`movb $0x39,0x42(%eax)` (0x39 = 57). The port had pinned the filter to
`model65 == 39 && tick70 != 62`, which is exactly the m57 lane, so an
m57 seeker could not have seen an m57 partner even without the
`is_fool` return. `sub_36F30` itself (file 0x5b73c-0x5b7a8, verified
instruction by instruction) is a tier contest on @0x46 with a coin flip
off the **survivor's own per-entity LCG** when the tiers tie and the
parents differ, then the loser's @0x28 / @0x94 / @0x46 / @0x2A move
across and it is hard-freed — no owner ladder anywhere.

**Measured, whole-take pair census on mc2l6-rsg:** (10,57) **657 → 173**
(−73.7%) — `mana` 113→0, `extra` 103→0, `f5a` 83→1, `applied_yaw` and
`applied_pitch` 82→0 each. Collateral, all improvements: **(9,9)
432 → 38**, (10,0) 509→415, (10,23) 56→3, (9,0) 622→605 — the fool's-mana
retaliation children the un-merged duplicate spheres kept minting.
Whole take **48,268 → 47,193**; conforming pairs 39,320 → 39,426.
**No family regressed and no pair became newly dirty**; **(3,0) is
3,100 → 3,100 exactly**, so the merge law is NOT upstream of the human's
pose family. Kept behind `MGC_NO_M57_MERGE=1` for A/B, house style.

FIXTURE: `the-fool-s-10-57-sphere-merges-with-its-own-merg` (mc2l6
t=10805) — GREEN under the law, **RED under `MGC_NO_M57_MERGE=1`** with
exactly the family's signature (`extra:10,57`, `field:10,57:mana`,
`f5a`, `applied_yaw`, `applied_pitch`) and no other fixture moving.

⭐ **PROCESS**: the dig's brief was refuted by its FIRST measurement,
which is the third wave running to do so. **Re-measure a banked head
before digging it** keeps earning its place.

### BANKED, VERIFIED AGAINST THE DECOMPILE, DELIBERATELY NOT LANDED

- ⭐⭐ **THE CLASS-10 `@0x2A` AMOUNT HOME IS MISSING TWO FAMILIES.**
  `sub_4F5F0` stamps `subSpellIndex_0x2A_42 = 25` on the (10,23) blast
  (EF:36087) and `sub_4F6A0` stamps 2000 on the (10,25) (EF:36117),
  while `sub_33D80` (EF:24796) deals `subSpellIndex_0x2A_42` — but the
  port's ctors write `f140` and `mc2_blast23_tick` reads `f140`, and
  neither model is in `import_ent_mc2`'s class-10 `@0x2A → f140`
  diversion list. So an IMPORTED blast reads the DEAD `@0x90` and deals
  **zero**, and a native one publishes the allocator's 100 on the graded
  `f2a` lane and 25 on `mana` where retail has 0. The fix follows the
  established per-family pattern (importer arm + the `f2a`/`mana`
  publish arms), and `obs_project_mc2` documents the tell in its own
  comment: *"a class-10 model outside it that the SIM stamps with an
  @0x2A amount reads ≠ against retail's dead 0 in this dump — which is
  the tell that its import case is missing, exactly how (10,17) was
  found."* ⏭ Audit the WHOLE class-10 ctor set the same way, not just
  these two.
- **THE LIGHTNING MARCH'S `for _ in 0..64` IS INVENTED.** Retail is
  `sub_66610(a1x); v27 = 1; while (!(byte[1] & 4)) { sub_66610(a1x);
  v27++; }` (EF:58306-14) — the first step is taken OUTSIDE the loop and
  the loop is UNBOUNDED. The port's step count agrees arm for arm; only
  the cap is fiction. ⚠ Needs a termination argument for
  `mc2_flyer_tick` before the cap comes off, or a hang replaces a
  divergence.
